rendered:
Yes. CD and UV–vis LODs are reported side by side for only a pair of strains, and CD is lower for both. The gap is large for P. aeruginosa and very small for L. monocytogenes.

- P. aeruginosa: CD LOD OD600 =0.0034[1], UV–vis LOD 0.0066[2]. CD is lower by 0.0032[3] OD600 units. That is about 48[4]% lower, roughly 1.9[5]-fold more sensitive.
- L. monocytogenes: CD LOD 0.0123[6], UV–vis LOD 0.0125[7]. CD is lower by only 0.0002[8] OD600 units, about 1.6[9]% lower. That is a marginal difference.

The paper states that CD consistently achieved lower limit of detection (LOD) than UV–vis[10]. That holds for both strains, but the size of the advantage varies a lot between them. E. coli and E. sakazakii were also tested across a concentration range, but no LOD values are given for them in this document. Their LOD figures, if any, would be in the supplementary material, which isn't included here.
